notes:
New in 0.2.0 - destruction lab (prototype of main phases 2 + 3, separate from the water for now):
- Press L on the beach to open it (L or Esc goes back). A street of random houses: cottage, town house, beach house on stilts, apartment block.
- Every house is built piece by piece: bricks, stones, timber boards and beams, roof tiles, concrete blocks, steel, metal sheet, glass panes. The pieces are held together by joints with real material strengths (mortar, nails, timber, rebar).
- Each frame the load in every joint is worked out (weight, impacts, water pressure, earthquake shaking). A joint that is overloaded cracks, bends (timber, steel, reinforced concrete) or breaks. Whatever is no longer held falls as real physics bodies: whole wall sections, roofs or single bricks.
- Glass shatters into shards, mortar and concrete give dust, timber splinters, plaster falls off and shows the brick behind.
- New lit look: sunlight on every pixel's surface, short relief shadows, see-through glass with the room behind and the sky reflected, the dark interior shows through broken windows and holes.
- Tools: 1 wrecking ball (drag back and let go), 2 bulldozer plate, 3 water pressure (stand-in for the sea, from the right), 4 remove supports (hold the mouse), 5 earthquake. Mouse wheel / Up / Down sets the strength. S stress view, T slow motion, P pause, R rebuild, N new street.
- Checked against hand calculations: a brick wall and a timber post under rising water fail within 3% of the engineering result. All 160 test houses stand under their own weight.
